title: Titanium Hypersonic Control Surface
alloyReason: Ti-65 near-alpha Ti alloy is engineered for this missile hardware high-temperature aero engine application capable of sustained operation at 600C - 100C above Ti-6Al-4V limits. Silicide precipitation provides creep resistance below 0.1% strain at 300 MPa/600C. This rationale is driven by hypersonic missile all-moving fin (ti-65) and service environment demands.

Wire EDM contour profiling with SPC sampling
CMM per AS9102 with SPC sampling

commonFailures: SCC in chloride-rich marine atmosphere - controlled by bake-out 300C + corrosion-inhibiting primer — critical for hypersonic missile allmoving performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Hypersonic Control Surface suitable for Hypersonic missile all-moving fin (Ti-65)?
faq.a: Titanium Hypersonic Control Surface uses Ti-65 because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address missile hardware operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Hypersonic Control Surface?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Hypersonic Control Surface is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for hypersonic missile allmoving requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Hypersonic Control Surface require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. hypersonic missile allmoving components require Shot peening Almen 0.008-0.012A inducing compressive residual stress for extended HCF life in aerospace service — tailored for hypersonic missile allmoving application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Hypersonic Control Surface shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Hypersonic Control Surface includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet hypersonic missile allmoving specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Control fin / Hypersonic rudder missile hardware components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
